messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate ΔS for heating from 0°C (ice) to 100°C water presumably. But we have phase changes: melting at 0°C then warming liquid water to 100°C. Also boiling maybe but not asked; just up to 100°C.

Assume constant pressure 1 atm. For reversible process, ΔS=∫C_p/T dT + latent heat terms / T. So:

ΔS_total = S_melt + ∫_0^100 C_water(T)/T dT - because starting at solid at 0°C? Actually start with ice at 0°C. We consider two steps:
1. Melt ice at 0°C: ΔS_phase = L_fus / T_initial where L_fus ~334 kJ/kg. At 273 K. So ΔS1 = 334000 J/kg / 273K ≈1222 J/K.
But careful sign positive since absorbing energy increases disorder.

2. Heat resulting water from 0°C to 100°C: integrate Cp_water over T. Use average cp about 4185 J/(kg·K). Integral gives Cp ln(373/273)=Cp*ln(373/273). Ln ratio approx ln(1.367)=0.313. Multiply by 4185 yields ~1310 J/K.

Total ΔS≈2532 J/K.

Thus answer around 2500 J/K. Provide explanation.
